the dynamic flow stress of pure Al at elevated temperatures is a result of the interplay of phonon drag restricted and thermally activated mechanisms for dislocation glide.

the dynamic flow stress of pure FCC metals is governed by the interplay of phonon drag restricted glide and thermally activated glide, which is a result of the evolution of the dislocation microstructure during plastic deformation.

the dynamic flow stress of polycrystaline aluminum is governed by the rate of dislocation accumulation and annihilation, and the extent to which the dislocation glide is restricted by phonon viscosity.

the Austin McDowell plasticity model, when extended to include a dynamic recovery term, is able to correlate the flow stress behavior of pure polycristalline aluminum in the strain rate and temperature ranges investigated.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the dislocation mediated plastic deformation models, in conjunction with the experimental observations of dynamic flow stress, provide a comprehensive framework to understand and predict the dynamic plastic flow of polycrystALLINE aluminum at incipient plastic deformation and elevated temperatures.

the dislocation mediated plastic flow model, when appropriately calibrated, can predict the flow stress of polycrystaline aluminum over the entire range of plastic strain rates and elevated temperatures studied.

the dislocation mediated plastic flow models are capable of predicting the dynamic flow stress of pure metals at large strains, provided they are calibrated to experimental data at small strains and are extended with new rate and temperature sensitive recovery mechanisms.
